**Strale delivers decision-ready outcomes for agents. Our first product, Counterparty Assurance, returns a complete counterparty answer in a single auditable call: identity, sanctions, ownership, bank verification.**
When an AI agent needs to decide something about a counterparty — whether to pay a supplier, whether a vendor is safe to onboard, whether a merchant is legitimate — it has to pull data from a dozen different sources, reconcile them, and work out whether what came back is enough to act on. The agent usually has no way to tell. Strale returns a single structured answer: the evidence, a decision-readiness signal that tells the agent whether the evidence is sufficient, and a hash-chained audit trail a regulator can inspect later.
Counterparty Assurance is the first product built on that model. Agents submit a counterparty (name, country, any identifiers they have), and Strale returns registry verification across EU and UK, tax and regulatory identifiers (VAT, LEI), bank account verification through IBAN/name matching, sanctions and PEP screening, beneficial ownership where available, entity resolution across all the identifiers the agent provided, and the decision-readiness object the agent uses to decide whether to proceed, flag for review, or block.
# Two surfaces, one company
Strale operates two public surfaces under Moonlighter AB. [**strale.io**](http://strale.io) is the home of Counterparty Assurance — the flagship product and Strale's commercial focus. Future Strale products may join [strale.io](http://strale.io) over time; their naming and framing will be decided when they launch. This is where Strale's marketing investment concentrates and where the bundled, audit-trail-bearing decision-ready outcomes are sold. [**strale.dev**](http://strale.dev) is the agent capabilities API: atomic capabilities exposed to agents and developers, priced per call, paid via x402, Stripe pre-paid balance, MPP, and Stripe Link for Agents. [strale.dev](http://strale.dev) gets less marketing investment than [strale.io](http://strale.io) but is not unmarketed — the audience differs, and so do the channels.
Both surfaces share one backend at [api.strale.io](http://api.strale.io), one billing infrastructure, one source-health substrate, and one set of capability integrations. The marketing surface splits by audience; the engineering surface stays unified.
Bundle pricing is enforced: for any capability that is a component of Counterparty Assurance, the standalone [strale.dev](http://strale.dev) price is set above the implicit per-call price within the bundle. A customer who needs the full counterparty answer finds the bundle cheaper than four marketplace calls. A customer who needs only one piece can buy it standalone, but at a price that reflects [strale.dev](http://strale.dev) being a substrate-display surface, not a price-competitive marketplace.
Deeper detail on each surface lives on its dedicated page: Strategy → "[strale.io](http://strale.io) — what it is and why" and Strategy → "[strale.dev](http://strale.dev) — what it is and why."
# Who we build for
Strale is for developers and teams building agents that need to decide something about a counterparty. AP automation agents. Partner onboarding agents. Due diligence research agents. B2B marketplace counterparty admission. Fintech builders with counterparty verification needs — payment platforms, marketplaces with KYB obligations, neobanks doing onboarding flows, lenders verifying business borrowers. The buyer is the person writing the integration code, not the finance team or the compliance officer downstream. Sales qualification, consumer-marketplace seller admission, and recurring-payment delta-checks need a thinner product tier than v1 ships and are deferred per DEC-20260502-A.
Compliance officers and risk leads at the same companies are the secondary audience. They're often the reason a buyer picks Strale over a wrapper, because the audit trail and provenance are what make the agent's decisions defensible when a regulator asks.
Strale is not for finance teams looking for dashboards, banks or PSPs building their own VOP infrastructure, hobbyists building demos, or teams optimising for cheapest-possible API calls regardless of where the data came from.
# Two customers, one platform
Long-term, Strale's customer is the production agent — autonomous, in deployment, making real decisions on behalf of a company that needs the audit trail. Short-term, Strale's customer is the developer building that agent — a human, currently choosing which tools to wire in before deployment. The two consume different things. The agent consumes decision-ready outcomes at runtime. The developer consumes documentation, MCP server listings, examples, and integration material.
Strale invests in both surfaces simultaneously because today's developer is the gatekeeper to tomorrow's production agent. As production agents become more common, the balance shifts toward the runtime side. The bridge changes shape over time; it does not disappear.
# Decision infrastructure underneath the products
Underneath Counterparty Assurance sits decision infrastructure for agent workflows — a horizontal substrate with six core capabilities: discovery (finding the right solution for the agent's question), routing (selecting the best source where alternatives exist; per-product, multi-attribute, fallback-aware per DEC-20260503-B), orchestration (combining many APIs into one call), entity resolution (reconciling identifiers across sources to produce a single high-confidence canonical entity), decision-readiness (the structured fields that tell the agent whether the evidence is sufficient to act), and audit trail (hash-chained provenance on every decision; tiered per DEC-20260503-B — basic call log on standalone capabilities, full regulator-ready audit trail on Counterparty Assurance and any future Strale product calls).
Counterparty Assurance is the first vertical product built on that substrate. Strale may build more vertical products on the same substrate over time — earned through customer pull or genuine strategic opportunity, not pushed by extending data coverage in new directions. Decisions about future products are deliberately deferred.
The same substrate also powers the agent capabilities API at [strale.dev](http://strale.dev). Every capability that is `marketplace_eligible` is exposed there atomically, priced per call, with a developer-honest health signal (uptime, last-verified, call volume) but no public quality scores or letter grades. SQS-as-public-score is retired (DEC-20260503-B); the substrate that powered it lives on as the source-health primitive feeding both surfaces.
# The structural bet
Strale runs the calls. That's the difference between Strale and an API directory, and it's what makes decision-ready outcomes possible at all. Directories list capabilities. Strale runs them, reconciles them, scores the evidence, and writes the audit trail. Entity resolution, decision-readiness, and cross-customer consistency detection all flow from being in the call path. None of them can be reproduced by listing capabilities or by reviewing them after the fact.
# What Strale is not
Strale is not a compliance product — sanctions screening, KYB, and PEP checks are components of decision-ready outcomes, not Strale's identity as a platform. Strale is not an identity layer — questions about who an agent is and who owns it belong to a different category (KYA providers). Strale is not an MCP tool rating service — MCP registries rate verbs; Strale delivers outcomes from data those verbs would need to be composed against. Strale is not committed to any single payment system — x402 is native for agent-native payment, Stripe handles human billing, MPP and Link for Agents are tracked as they mature, and whatever else gets traction will be supported. Strale only uses direct data connections — government registries via official APIs, licensed data providers under contract, or open standards. No scraping, full ToS compliance with every provider.
# The pitch line
*Strale delivers decision-ready outcomes for agents. Our first product, Counterparty Assurance, returns a complete counterparty answer in a single auditable call: identity, sanctions, ownership, bank verification.*
